matters.title: Lakewood Park Regional Park Pool Aquifer Wells and Submersible Pump Installation - $60,544.00
matters.text: The Aquifer geothermal pool heating system supply and return wells at the Lakewood Park Regional Park Aquatic facility need to be replaced. The wells are no longer operable and have met the end of their useful life. Contractor Symbiont Service, the manufacturer of the heater/chiller unit, provided the County with a proposal in the amount of $60,5440. This proposal includes the electrical wiring and water piping, the delivery and installation of (2) new Aquifer Wells and the installation of a new submersible well pump. Replacing the wells will offer the heater/chiller unit more energy efficiency by using the infinite energy source, this allows the geothermal heater/chiller to operate efficiently and effectively all year-round. Once the Aquifer wells and pump is installed, the heater/chiller unit will be operational, allowing the Aquatic facility to meet the demands for pool programming, increase pool operations, and improve public infrastructure, which will enhance public safety and benefit the overall well-being for the County's residents.

matters.title: Sole Source Radio Replacement for Transit Vehicles
matters.text:
The Transit Department is requesting a sole source procurement for purchase, installation and updated radios for the transit vehicles. The existing radio system for the transit vehicles was purchased from and installed by Motorola. The hardware, software, and system design for this system is proprietary; therefore, all other vendors that provide this type of service would require Transit to purchase their hardware and software. In order to maintain continuity and connectivity across the system, it is in the best interest and best value for Transit to move forward with this purchase. 
The radio system is critical to the daily functions of the transit system. The replacement/upgrade of this system will ensure critical service provision and good customer service. The cost for this will be $386,727.19. This sole-source-purchase is the most cost-effective way to replace the radios and ensure connectivity with the existing system.

matters.title: Purchase of Aluminum Telescopic Mobile Tower Trailer and Radio Communications Equipment for Public Safety Communications
matters.text:
Bid No. 24-057 was opened on May 15, 2024 for interested parties to submit proposals for one (1) aluminum telescopic mobile tower trailer to be part of the County's Rapid Emergency Deployable Communications (REDCOMMS) project, which is a self-contained mobile communications system consisting of a trailer, tower, generator, and radio equipment system designed to be rapidly deplorable and serve as a backup in th event our current 800MHz radio system becomes inoperable.
Out of the 91 companies notified, nine (9) received bid documents and only one (1) bid was received, from Aluma Tower with a bid price of $130,189.25.
In addition to the trailer, Motorola Solutions, as the sole source vendor of our current Public Safety Communications system will retrofit the tower trailer with communications equipment to include all necessary software, hardware, and installation services of six (6) P25 conventional repeaters in 700MHz with a price of $166,193.84.

matters.text:
The Information Technology Department is continuing its efforts to standardize and modernize the County's security infrastructure across all sites for The Board of County Commissioners. In fiscal year 2024, the Keri Access Control security system was installed county-wide. However, the Digital Watchdog closed circuit television system (CCTV) camera system was installed at only approximately 25% of Board of County Commissioner sites. The ultimate goal for the county is to replace all legacy CCTV cameras with the standardized Digital Watchdog system which will seamlessly integrate with the Keri Access Control security system. The Keri Access Control system is designed with flexibility and interoperability in mind, enabling smooth integration with a variety of gate automation systems. Through advanced relay modules and programming options, Keri Access Control systems can control and monitor gate access points efficiently. The Keri Access Control system software is compatible with DW Spectrum™ IPVMS, creating a unified platform for access control and video surveillance.This integration delivers the following advantages: event-based recording, enhanced monitoring and streamlined investigations.
On February 18, 2025 Gearface, LLC was granted a sole source agreement by the Board of County Commissioners. We are seeking sole source approval for another year with Gearface, LLC for items related to the Keri Access Control System and Digital Watchdog integration. Per a letter received from Keri System, Gearface, LLC is the sole integrator in the Treasure Coast geographical area that is a Keri partner through their Integrated Partner Program (IPP).
We recommend utilizing a single vendor to install and maintain the system, including Keri Access Control and DW Spectrum™ IPVMS. Working with a single vendor ensures unified support, seamless integration, cost efficiency and consistency in quality. We believe this approach aligns with the county's goals for enhanced security, streamlined operations, and cost-effective system management.
